q: What is the minimum age for a Florida learner's license?
exp: Florida issues a learner's license at 15 to an applicant who meets the other requirements.
src: Fla. Stat. 322.1615(1); flhsmv.gov, Licensing Requirements for Teens, Graduated Driver License Laws and Driving Curfews

q: How many questions are on the Florida Class E Knowledge Exam?
exp: The Class E Knowledge Exam has 50 multiple choice questions.
src: flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test; Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 20

q: How many questions must you answer correctly to pass the Florida Class E Knowledge Exam?
exp: You must answer 40 of the 50 questions correctly, which is 80 percent.
src: flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test

q: Who must ride with a Florida learner's license holder?
a: Any licensed driver at least 18, in any seat
b: A licensed driver at least 21, in the front seat to the driver's right
c: A parent of any age, in the back seat
d: A licensed driver at least 25, in any front seat
exp: The supervisor must be licensed, at least 21, and sit in the front seat closest to the driver's right.
src: Fla. Stat. 322.1615(2); Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 25

q: During the first three months, when may a Florida learner's license holder drive?
d: At any hour with a supervisor
exp: For the first three months a learner may drive only in daylight; after that, until 10 p.m.

q: After holding a learner's license for three months, a Florida learner may drive until what time?
exp: After three months, a learner may drive until 10 p.m., always with a licensed supervisor 21 or older.
src: Fla. Stat. 322.1615(3); flhsmv.gov, Licensing Requirements for Teens, Graduated Driver License Laws and Driving Curfews

q: How many hours of supervised driving must a Florida driver under 18 have certified before getting a Class E license?
a: 40 hours, including at least 5 at night
b: 65 hours, including at least 10 at night
d: 50 hours, including at least 10 at night
exp: A parent, guardian or responsible adult 21 or older certifies at least 50 hours of driving, 10 of them at night.
src: flhsmv.gov, Licensing Requirements for Teens, Graduated Driver License Laws and Driving Curfews; Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 8

q: Unless driving directly to or from work, a 16-year-old Florida license holder may not drive alone between:
exp: A 16-year-old may drive alone from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; at other times a licensed driver 21 or older must ride along, unless driving to or from work.
src: Fla. Stat. 322.16(2); flhsmv.gov, Licensing Requirements for Teens, Graduated Driver License Laws and Driving Curfews

q: Unless driving directly to or from work, a 17-year-old Florida license holder may not drive alone between:
exp: At 17, the restricted hours are 1 a.m. to 5 a.m., unless a licensed driver 21 or older rides along or the trip is to or from work.
src: Fla. Stat. 322.16(3); flhsmv.gov, Licensing Requirements for Teens, Graduated Driver License Laws and Driving Curfews

q: A Florida driver under 18 who collects 6 or more points within 12 months is:
b: Restricted to driving for business purposes only for one year
c: Required to retake the knowledge exam
exp: Drivers under 18 with 6 or more points in 12 months are automatically restricted to Business Purposes Only for one year.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 29

q: Under 18, how long must you hold a Florida learner's license before getting a Class E license?
a: 12 months, or until you turn 18 if that comes first
exp: A minor must hold the learner's license 12 months or until the 18th birthday, whichever comes first.
src: flhsmv.gov, Licensing Requirements for Teens, Graduated Driver License Laws and Driving Curfews; Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 8

q: Who may certify a Florida teen's 50 hours of driving experience?
c: The teen, by signing a log
d: A parent, legal guardian or responsible adult 21 or older
exp: The Certification of Minor Driving Experience is completed by a parent, legal guardian or a responsible adult 21 or older.
src: flhsmv.gov, Licensing Requirements for Teens, Graduated Driver License Laws and Driving Curfews

q: Which age group may take the Florida Class E Knowledge Exam online?
c: Only applicants who hold a license from another country
exp: Only applicants under 18 may take the knowledge exam online, through an approved third-party administrator.
src: flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test; flhsmv.gov, Teen Licensing FAQ

q: A Florida teen who takes the knowledge exam online needs which form signed by a parent?
a: The Certification of Minor Driving Experience
exp: Online testing requires a Parent Proctoring Form, notarized or signed in front of a driver license examiner.
src: flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test; flhsmv.gov, Teen Licensing FAQ

q: In what language is the Florida knowledge exam given?
d: Any language, with a translation device
exp: FLHSMV now gives all driver license exams in English only and has removed translation services.
src: FLHSMV policy, exams in English only (reported by Hillsborough County Tax Collector and WUSF, Jan. 30)

q: What must a Florida applicant under 18 complete before getting a learner's license?
a: A driver education course approved by FLHSMV
d: A 6-hour behind-the-wheel lesson with an examiner
exp: A learner's license applicant must complete an approved driver education course that meets the state classroom course standard.
src: Fla. Stat. 322.1615(1)(c) (2026 Statutes)

q: A first-time Florida applicant who is 18 or older and has never held a license must complete which course?
a: The Traffic Law and Substance Abuse Education (TLSAE) course
exp: Applicants 18 or older must complete TLSAE unless they were licensed in another jurisdiction or passed a Department of Education driver education course.
src: Fla. Stat. 322.095(1) (2026 Statutes)

q: What is the minimum length of the Florida TLSAE course?
exp: The TLSAE course must include at least 4 hours of course content.
src: Fla. Stat. 322.095(9) (2026 Statutes)

q: What does the original Florida Class E fee of $48 include?
exp: FLHSMV lists the original Class E fee as $48, including the learner's license.
src: flhsmv.gov/fees

q: How much does it cost to retake the Florida Class E Knowledge Exam?
exp: Each knowledge exam retest costs $10, plus a service fee at tax collector offices.
src: flhsmv.gov/fees; Fla. Stat. 322.12(1)

q: How much does it cost to retake the Florida driving skills test?
exp: Each driving skills retest costs $20, plus a service fee at tax collector offices.
src: flhsmv.gov/fees; Fla. Stat. 322.12(1)

q: What extra fee may a tax collector office add to a Florida license transaction?
exp: An additional $6.25 service fee may apply to credentials issued at a tax collector office.
src: flhsmv.gov/fees

q: How many documents showing your Florida home address must you bring when you apply?
exp: Every applicant for a license or ID card presents two documents with a Florida residential address.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 7

q: Which copy of a birth certificate will a Florida service center accept as primary identification?
c: A certified copy issued by a government agency
d: A clear photo on your phone
exp: Documents must be originals or certified; hospital birth certificates and notarized copies are not accepted.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), pp. 5 to 7

q: Who may sign the parental consent form for an unmarried Florida applicant under 18?
b: A stepparent who has not adopted the child
c: A parent or legal guardian, in front of the agent or a notary
exp: A parent or legal guardian signs before the license agent or a notary; a stepparent may sign only after legal adoption.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 8; flhsmv.gov, Teen Licensing FAQ

q: What happens if the adult who signed a Florida minor's consent form withdraws it?
a: The minor must retake the knowledge exam
exp: The signer accepts responsibility for the minor's driving; if the signer rescinds it, the license is canceled.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), pp. 8 to 9

q: What vision result in each eye meets Florida's standard without a referral to an eye specialist?
exp: Vision of 20/40 or better in each eye, with or without lenses, meets the standard without referral.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 19

q: What is the minimum field of vision for a Florida driver?
exp: The minimum acceptable field of vision for an applicant or licensed driver is 130 degrees.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 19

q: If you need glasses to pass the Florida vision test, what appears on your license?
exp: Code B means you must wear glasses or contacts whenever you drive.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 10

q: What moving violation record must a Florida driver under 18 have before getting a Class E license?
b: No convictions in the last 3 months only
c: No convictions in the 12 months after the learner's license was issued
d: Violations do not matter for a Class E license
exp: There must be no moving violation convictions for 12 months from issue; one is allowed only if adjudication was withheld.
src: flhsmv.gov, Licensing Requirements for Teens, Graduated Driver License Laws and Driving Curfews; Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 8

q: Who may ride along so a 16-year-old Florida driver can drive after 11 p.m.?
d: Any passenger with a learner's license
exp: The curfew exception requires a licensed driver at least 21, or driving directly to or from work.

q: Which trip is an exception to the Florida teen driver curfew?
a: Driving directly to or from work
b: Driving home from a friend's house
exp: Travel directly to or from work is an exception for both 16- and 17-year-olds.

q: How many points does driving during restricted hours add to a Florida driving record?
exp: Driving during restricted hours is a 3-point violation.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 30

q: A Florida driver under 18 is restricted to Business Purposes Only and then gets more points. What happens?
b: The restriction ends at 18 no matter what
c: Nothing; extra points do not count
d: The restriction grows by 90 days for each additional point
exp: Each additional point extends the restriction by 90 days.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 29

q: When may a Florida driver under 18 take the Class E driving skills test?
a: After holding a learner's license 3 months
c: After holding a learner's license 12 months
d: After 6 months if 50 hours are logged
exp: Applicants must hold a learner's license 12 months or be 18 years old.
src: flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test

q: Who may ride in the car during a Florida driving skills test?
b: No one but the examiner, unless an interpreter is needed
exp: No other passengers are permitted during the exam unless a language interpreter is necessary.
src: flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test; Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 20

q: How far must you back up during the Florida driving skills test?
exp: You back up 50 feet slowly while looking to the rear, without using mirrors or the camera.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 20; flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test

q: A new Florida driver who is 18 or older:
a: Does not need a learner's license first
b: Must hold a learner's license 12 months
exp: First-time drivers 18 or older are not required to obtain a learner's license.
src: Palm Beach County Tax Collector, New Drivers Aged 18 or Older; flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test

q: How long does a new Florida resident have to get a Florida driver license?
exp: A new resident, or a non-resident who takes a job or enrolls a child in public school, must get a Florida license within 30 days.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 3; Palm Beach County Tax Collector, Transfer Driver License

q: A new Florida resident with a valid license from another U.S. state usually must take which test?
a: The knowledge exam and skills test
exp: Knowledge and skills tests are waived for a valid license from a U.S. state; the vision exam is still required.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 4; Fla. Stat. 322.12(1)

q: A new Florida resident with a valid driver license from Germany must take which exam?
c: The knowledge exam (the skills test is waived)
exp: Florida waives only the driving skills test for a German license; the knowledge and vision exams are required.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 4

q: A new Florida resident with a license from a country with no Florida agreement, such as Brazil, must:
b: Pass both the knowledge exam and the skills test
exp: Exams are waived only for listed jurisdictions; other license holders must take both exams.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 4; Palm Beach County Tax Collector, Transfer Driver License

q: What is the standard school zone speed limit in Florida?
exp: Florida's standard school zone limit is 20 mph during posted times or while the light flashes.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), pp. 57, 68

q: What happens to a speeding fine in a Florida school zone or construction zone?
exp: Fines are doubled for speeding in a school zone or construction zone.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 29

q: In Florida, holding a phone while driving through a school zone is:
a: Legal if you are not texting
b: A nonmoving violation with no points
exp: Using a handheld wireless device in a school zone, school crossing or work zone is a moving violation worth 3 points.
src: Fla. Stat. 316.306; HB 107 (2019) final analysis; Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 30

q: When does the ban on holding a phone apply in a Florida work zone?
b: Only when a police car is present
c: When construction workers are present or operating equipment
d: Never; work zones are not covered
exp: The handheld ban covers work zones when construction personnel are present or operating equipment on or next to the road.
src: Fla. Stat. 316.306; HB 107 (2019) final analysis

q: What do the words BEGIN SCHOOL ZONE tell a Florida driver?
a: School is closed for the day
b: Do not exceed the school zone limit during posted times or when the light flashes
exp: Do not exceed the school zone speed limit during indicated times or when the light is flashing.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 57

q: What is the maximum civil penalty for speeding in a Florida school or construction zone?
exp: Doubled school and construction zone fines can reach civil penalties up to $1,000.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 29

q: Which Florida law also protects road and bridge maintenance or construction vehicles stopped with warning lights?
exp: Florida's Move Over law covers road and bridge maintenance or construction vehicles displaying warning lights.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 65

q: How many points does the Florida handbook list for using a handheld device in a work zone?
exp: Using a handheld device in a school crossing, school zone or work zone carries 3 points.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 30

q: In Florida, may you turn right on a steady red light?
b: Yes, without stopping if no one is coming
c: Yes, after a full stop, if no sign forbids it and the way is clear
d: Only when a green arrow also shows
exp: After stopping, you may turn right on red unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted, yielding to pedestrians and traffic.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 51

q: In Florida, when may you turn left on a steady red light?
b: From a one-way street onto a one-way street with traffic moving left
d: Only from a two-way street onto a one-way street
exp: A left on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street whose traffic moves to the left, after a full stop.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 51

q: In Florida, what may you do at a steady red arrow after a full stop, if no sign forbids it?
a: Nothing until the arrow turns green
b: Turn right, or turn left from one-way onto one-way
exp: The handbook allows the same right turn and one-way to one-way left turn on a red arrow, after stopping and yielding.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 52

q: Before turning on red in Florida, you must yield to:
a: Pedestrians in the crosswalk and oncoming traffic
exp: Before a turn on red, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to other traffic.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 51

q: What should you do at a Florida intersection with a broken traffic signal and no officer present?
b: Treat it as a yield sign
d: Treat it as a four-way stop
exp: If a signal is out and no officer is present, treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 51

q: What does a NO TURN ON RED sign forbid in Florida?
c: Turning right or left while the light is red
exp: With this sign, you must wait for the green signal before turning.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 48

q: On a Florida multi-lane road, what must you do when approaching a stopped tow truck with warning lights on?
c: Move out of the lane closest to it, or slow to 20 mph below the limit if you cannot
exp: Vacate the closest lane when safe; if you cannot, slow to 20 mph below the posted limit.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 65

q: On a Florida two-lane road posted at 55 mph, how fast may you pass a stopped police car with lights flashing?
exp: On a two-lane road you must slow to 20 mph below the posted limit, so 55 becomes 35.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 65

q: Under Florida's Move Over law, how fast must you go past a stopped emergency vehicle where the limit is 20 mph?
exp: Where the posted limit is 20 mph or less, you must slow to 5 mph.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 65

q: Does Florida's Move Over law cover a disabled car with its hazard lights on?
exp: The law covers disabled vehicles showing hazard lights, flares or signs, or with people visibly present.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 65

q: On a Florida two-lane road, a school bus stops with red lights flashing and stop arm out. Who must stop?
c: No one, if no children are visible
exp: On a two-way road, traffic in both directions stops until the stop arm is withdrawn.
src: flhsmv.gov, School Bus Safety; Fla. Stat. 316.172(1)

q: When may oncoming Florida traffic keep moving past a stopped school bus?
a: On any road with four lanes
b: On any road with a painted center line
c: On a divided highway with a raised median, barrier, or unpaved median at least 5 feet wide
exp: Oncoming drivers need not stop on a divided highway with an unpaved space of at least 5 feet, a raised median or a physical barrier.
src: Fla. Stat. 316.172(2); flhsmv.gov, School Bus Safety

q: How many points does passing a stopped school bus add to a Florida driving record?
exp: Passing a stopped school bus is a 4-point violation, and also requires a basic driver improvement course.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), pp. 27, 30

q: What is the minimum fine in Florida for passing a stopped school bus on the side where children get on and off?
exp: The minimum fine is $265, rising to $465 when passing on the side where children enter and exit.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 27; flhsmv.gov, School Bus Safety

q: When may a Florida driver move again after stopping for a school bus?
a: When the stop signal is withdrawn
c: As soon as the doors close
exp: You may not pass until the bus withdraws its stop signal.

q: Under Florida law, how close may you follow a fire truck answering an alarm?
c: Any distance if you keep pace
exp: It is illegal to follow a fire truck responding to an emergency closer than 500 feet.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 62

q: How far before a turn must Florida drivers begin signaling?
exp: Florida requires a turn signal at least 100 feet before the turn.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 69

q: Where is a U-turn never allowed in Florida?
a: On a residential street with good visibility
c: At a wide intersection with no sign
d: In a multi-lane roundabout from the left lane
exp: Never make a U-turn or three-point turn on a curve, a hill, the highway, or where a sign forbids it.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 70

q: In a Florida multi-lane roundabout, which lane do you use for a U-turn?
exp: To go straight or left, or make a U-turn, use the left lane.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 63

q: In Florida, using your turn signal to tell the driver behind you to pass is:
exp: It is against the law to use directional signals to tell drivers behind you that they can pass.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 69

q: From which side of a car are Florida hand signals given?
exp: Hand signals must be given from the left side of the vehicle.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 69

q: If you miss your exit on a Florida limited access highway, you should:
b: Make a U-turn through the median
c: Go on to the next exit
d: Stop and wait for a gap
exp: Never back up or cross the median; continue to the next exit.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), pp. 64 to 65

q: In Florida, a three-point turn should be used only when:
c: The road is too narrow for a U-turn and you cannot go around the block
exp: Use a three-point turn only if the road is too narrow for a U-turn and you can't go around the block.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 70

q: When does Florida require a turn signal besides at turns?
a: Only when other cars are present
b: When changing lanes or overtaking a vehicle
exp: Signals are required by law when changing lanes or overtaking a vehicle.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 69

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Florida business or residential area?
exp: Florida's standard limit for municipal, business or residential areas is 30 mph.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 68

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on Florida streets and highways outside towns?
exp: The standard limit on streets and highways is 55 mph.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 68

q: What is the highest speed limit allowed anywhere in Florida?
exp: In Florida the speed limit will never be higher than 70 mph.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), pp. 28, 68

q: On a Florida highway posted at 70 mph, what is the minimum speed?
exp: When the posted limit is 70 mph, the minimum speed limit is 50 mph.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 68

q: Is driving up to 10 mph over the limit allowed in Florida?
b: No; any speed over the limit can be ticketed
exp: The handbook calls the speeding buffer a myth; you may be cited for any speed over the limit.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 68

q: How many points does Florida add for going 16 mph or more over the limit?
exp: Speeding 15 mph or less over is 3 points; 16 or more over is 4 points.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 30

q: How many points does Florida add for speeding that causes a crash?
exp: Unlawful speed resulting in a crash is a 6-point violation.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 30

q: Under Florida's dangerous excessive speeding law, driving how far over the limit is a crime?
exp: Driving 50 mph or more over the limit, or 100 mph or more in a way that threatens others, is dangerous excessive speeding.
src: Fla. Stat. 316.1922; ch. 2025-77, Laws of Fla.

q: What is the maximum jail time for a first conviction of dangerous excessive speeding in Florida?
exp: A first conviction carries up to 30 days in jail, a $500 fine, or both.
src: Fla. Stat. 316.1922; ch. 2025-77, Laws of Fla.

q: What following distance does the Florida handbook recommend in good weather?
exp: Keep a minimum following distance of four seconds in favorable weather and traffic.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 61

q: Using the Florida counting method, you reach the marker before you finish counting to four. You should:
exp: If you pass the marker before four seconds, you are too close; reduce speed and recount.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 61

q: In Florida, which vehicles may use an HOV lane?
a: Vehicles with two or more occupants, or decaled hybrid or low emission vehicles
d: Only vehicles with three or more people
exp: HOV lanes are reserved for vehicles with two or more occupants or hybrid and low emission vehicles with a decal.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 69

q: Where may you enter or leave a Florida HOV lane?
exp: Vehicles may enter and exit the HOV lane only at designated points.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 69

q: How is a Florida HOV lane usually marked?
a: With a solid yellow line on the right
c: With signs and diamond symbols, separated by a striped buffer
exp: HOV lanes are identified by signs and diamond pavement symbols and separated by a striped buffer zone.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 69

q: In Florida, how close to a fire hydrant may you park?
exp: Florida bans parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 66

q: In Florida, you may not park within how many feet of an intersection?
exp: Parking within 20 feet of an intersection is against the law.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 66

q: In Florida, you may not park within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
exp: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 66

q: In Florida, you may not park within how many feet of a stop sign or traffic signal?
exp: Parking within 30 feet of a flashing signal, stop sign or traffic signal is banned.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 66

q: When parallel parking in Florida, your curbside wheels must be within:
exp: Park parallel with the right wheels within 12 inches of the curb or side of the roadway.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 65

q: What does Florida law require you to do with your keys when you leave your parked car?
a: Leave them in the ignition for towing
c: Take them out of the vehicle
d: Leave them with the engine running
exp: Florida law requires you to take the keys out before leaving the vehicle.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 65

q: In Florida, you may not park within how many feet of the entrance to a fire station?
exp: Do not park within 20 feet of the entrance to a fire, ambulance or rescue station.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 66

q: Which place is a legal parking spot in Florida?
a: A marked space 40 feet from a hydrant on a quiet street
exp: Florida bans parking in bike lanes, by yellow curbs and on bridges; a marked space well clear of a hydrant is allowed.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 66

q: How much space must you leave when passing a bicycle in Florida?
exp: Florida requires at least 3 feet when passing a bicycle.

q: In Florida, if you cannot pass a cyclist with 3 feet of space, you must:
a: Honk so the cyclist moves over
b: Pass anyway at a slow speed
exp: If a 3-foot pass is not possible, remain behind the cyclist until it is.

q: May a Florida driver cross a double yellow line to pass a bicyclist?
c: Yes, briefly, when it is safe
exp: Drivers may briefly go left of center, even at double yellow lines, to pass a bicyclist when safe.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), pp. 43 to 44

q: When a Florida driver turns across a bike lane, the driver must:
b: Yield to bicyclists in the lane
c: Drive in the bike lane for 100 feet
exp: Motor vehicles may cross a bike lane to turn only when no cyclist is present, yielding to bicyclists.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), pp. 45, 70

q: When entering a Florida right turn lane that has bicyclists going straight, you must:
c: Expect them to yield to you
exp: When entering a right turn lane you must yield to bicyclists traveling straight.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 47

q: How much space does Florida require when passing a cyclist riding in a marked bike lane?
exp: Drivers must keep at least 3 feet from a bicycle in a bicycle lane.

q: In Florida, when must you switch to low beams for an oncoming vehicle?
exp: Florida requires dimming within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

q: In Florida, when must you switch to low beams while following another vehicle?
exp: When within 300 feet of a vehicle ahead, do not use high beams.

q: When you turn on your windshield wipers in Florida, you should also:
exp: The handbook says to turn on headlights whenever you turn on windshield wipers.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), pp. 71 to 72

q: In Florida, a crash with no injuries causes about $2,500 in damage. Must you notify police?
a: No, only injury crashes are reported
b: Yes, damage of $2,000 or more must be reported
c: Only if a car is towed
exp: Drivers must immediately notify law enforcement of a crash with injury, death, or damage of $2,000 or more.
src: Fla. Stat. 316.065(1); SB 488 (effective Oct. 1)

q: After a Florida crash with only property damage, your car is blocking traffic. You should:
a: Make every reasonable effort to move it out of the way
b: Leave it in place until police arrive
exp: If a damaged vehicle obstructs traffic, the driver must make every reasonable effort to move it.

q: In fog or heavy smoke in Florida, which lights should you use?
exp: High beams reflect off fog; drive with low beams, and parking lights are not a substitute.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 71

q: What must a Florida driver do immediately after a crash?
a: Drive home and report it later
b: Stop only if someone is injured
d: Stop at or as close to the scene as possible
exp: A driver in a crash must immediately stop at the scene or as close to it as possible.

q: What is the legal BAC limit for Florida drivers 21 and older?
exp: Your license is administratively suspended at a BAL of 0.08 or above.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 25

q: A Florida driver under 21 is stopped with a BAC of 0.02. What happens?
b: The license is suspended for six months
exp: Under 21, a BAL of 0.02 or higher brings an automatic six-month suspension.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 26

q: A Florida driver under 21 with a BAC of 0.05 or higher must also:
exp: Any driver under 21 with a BAL of 0.05 or higher must attend a substance abuse course.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 26

q: What happens the first time you refuse a breath, blood or urine test in Florida?
a: Your license is suspended for one year
b: Nothing, if you are not convicted
exp: A refusal brings an automatic one-year suspension.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 26

q: In Florida, a second refusal to take a breath, blood or urine test brings:
d: An 18-month suspension and a first-degree misdemeanor
exp: A second refusal results in an 18-month suspension and a first-degree misdemeanor.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 26

q: How many days do you have after a Florida DUI arrest to request a review of the administrative suspension?
exp: You must apply for a formal or informal review hearing within 10 days of the arrest.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 31

q: What is the license penalty for a first DUI conviction in Florida?
exp: A first DUI brings license revocation of at least 180 days.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 26

q: What is the fine range for a first Florida DUI conviction with a BAC under 0.15 and no minor in the car?
exp: A first DUI fine is $500 to $1,000, rising to $1,000 to $2,000 at 0.15 or with a minor in the vehicle.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 26

q: How long does a DUI conviction stay on a Florida driving record?
exp: A DUI conviction must remain on your driving record for 75 years.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 35

q: Under Florida law, may a passenger in a private car drink from an open container of alcohol while the car is driven?
a: Yes, only the driver is banned
b: Yes, if the passenger is over 21
c: Yes, if the container is in the back seat
d: No, drivers and passengers are both banned
exp: Both operators and passengers are prohibited from possessing an open container or drinking in a moving vehicle.

q: In Florida, can police stop you just for texting while driving?
c: Yes, it is a primary offense
exp: Since the law changed to primary enforcement, an officer may stop a driver solely for texting.
src: HB 107 (2019) final analysis; Fla. Stat. 316.305

q: What is the penalty for a first Florida texting-while-driving offense?
c: A nonmoving violation with a $30 fine plus costs
exp: A first offense is a nonmoving violation, $30 plus court costs; a second within five years is moving, 3 points.
src: HB 107 (2019) final analysis; Fla. Stat. 316.305

q: A second Florida texting offense within five years brings:
b: 3 points and a $60 fine plus costs
exp: A second offense within five years is a moving violation with three points and a $60 fine plus costs.
src: HB 107 (2019) final analysis

q: Does the Florida texting ban apply while your car is stopped?
a: No, it applies while the vehicle is moving
b: Yes, at all times in the car
c: Yes, but only at red lights
exp: Neither the texting ban nor the handheld ban applies to a stationary vehicle.
src: HB 107 (2019) final analysis

q: For a first Florida DUI, how much community service is required?
exp: A first conviction includes 50 hours of community service.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 26

q: Under Florida law, which passengers must wear seat belts?
d: Front seat passengers and all passengers under 18
exp: Florida requires belts for the driver, front seat passengers and passengers under 18.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 28

q: A 16-year-old rides unbelted in the back seat of a Florida car. Who is charged?
d: No one, back seat belts are optional
exp: The driver is charged if any passenger under 18 is not properly restrained.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 28

q: A 30-year-old front seat passenger in Florida is not belted. Who is charged?
exp: Passengers 18 or older are charged themselves when they fail to wear a required belt.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 28

q: In Florida, a child under age 4 must ride in:
c: A booster seat or seat belt
d: The front seat with an adult
exp: Children under 4 must be in a safety seat.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 28

q: In Florida, a 5-year-old riding with a parent must be in:
a: A child safety seat or a booster seat
exp: Children ages 4 and 5 must be in a safety seat or booster seat.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 28

q: Where should a rear-facing child seat never be placed?
c: In the middle of the back seat
exp: Never place a rear-facing car seat in front of an airbag.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 28

q: What minimum Property Damage Liability coverage must Florida car owners carry?
exp: Florida requires at least $10,000 PIP and $10,000 PDL.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 23

q: If a Florida driver's insurance lapses and new proof is not provided, the license and plate can be suspended for up to:
exp: Failing to provide proof of new insurance can suspend your license and plate for up to three years.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 23

q: Within how many days must you update your address after moving within Florida?
exp: You must obtain a new license within 30 calendar days of an address change.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 12

q: A non-resident who starts a job in Florida must register their car within:
exp: Non-residents who accept employment or enroll children in public school must register within 10 days.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 37

q: On the Florida driving skills test, how big a space do you have for a three-point turn?
exp: The three-point turn is done in a 20 to 40 foot space.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 21; flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test

q: When backing 50 feet on the Florida driving skills test, you should:
c: Look to the rear, without using mirrors or the backup camera
d: Back up quickly to save time
exp: Back up slowly while looking to the rear; do not use the rear-view mirror or camera monitor.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 20

q: What following distance does the Florida driving skills test score?
exp: The skills test checks a minimum following distance of four seconds.
src: flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test

q: Which car would be turned away from a Florida driving skills test?
d: A car with a backup camera
exp: The test is not given if the tag is expired, among other defects.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 20; flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test

q: On the Florida driving skills test, straight-in parking is correct when:
a: The car is centered in the space with no part in the traffic lane
c: The front bumper touches the curb
d: The car is angled for an easy exit
exp: The vehicle should be centered inside the space with no part extending into the traffic lane.
src: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 21

q: You passed the Florida knowledge exam with a third-party administrator. FLHSMV may:
c: Require a new driver education course
d: Randomly retest you at an office for free
exp: Third-party passers may be randomly selected for a no-fee mandatory retest without notice.
src: flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test; Fla. Stat. 322.56(3)

q: What must the car you bring to the Florida driving skills test have?
d: Valid registration and proof of insurance
exp: You must provide a vehicle with valid registration and insurance; the examiner inspects it.
src: flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test; Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), p. 20

q: After you pass the Florida driving skills test, what happens to your learner's license?
b: It is mailed back to you
c: You surrender it for your Class E license
d: It stays valid for another year
exp: After passing, you surrender the learner's license at a service center to receive the Class E license.
src: flhsmv.gov, Class E Knowledge Exam and Driving Skills Test; flhsmv.gov, Teen Licensing FAQ
